newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER ON MONDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were indicated softer in fairly quiet trade on Monday despite a slight cash shortage in the system, dealers said.

"We opened Z$136 million in surplus but the market is a little bit short at the moment because we have had more outflows than inflows and there are not many treasury bill maturities from the (central) Reserve Bank today," a dealer said.

Discount houses were on Monday selling treasury bills at 17.85 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18.50 and 17.85 (buying and selling respectively) from Friday's 18.50 and 18 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were at 18.50 and 18.25 percent from 19 percent and 18.5 percent but call money was indicated firmer at 18 percent from 17.50 percent.
